title.narrative: Output A.1. Enhanced decent work statistics using innovative sources and statistical standards

description.narrative: In 2017, Samoa implemented its second Labour Force Survey alongside the School To Work Transition Survey. These important national surveys provided useful information on Samoa’s Labour market which further assisted in policy decision-making, updating Samoa's national voluntary report, and were further used as a baseline for situational analysis for Samoa, mainly on unemployment and forecasting the labour market situation in Samoa and the Pacific Region. Since 2017, there has been hardly any other good data that can determine the trend of the Samoan economy which was also affected by the Measle Outbreak in late 2019, and COVID-19 2020. Most of the evidence-based data collection at the moment to assist with programme and policy advice was mainly from the Rapid Assessment Samoa conducted in 2020 on the impact of COVID-19 on employment and enterprises. Samoa successfully conducted its 3rd LFC in 2022 with technical assistance from the ILO collecting much-needed and up-to-date data on Samoa’s current employment status to inform decision making in Samoa. The ILO provided technical and financial assistance in the collection of the Labour Force Survey in Samoa as well as critical analytical support towards the analysis of the LFS data in doing so strengthening labour market statistics and information systems using international statistical standards which also enhanced the reporting on the SDG Global Indicator Framework.
